subject: Granular acceptance & lead-time alignment for capacity reservation

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Granular acceptance & lead-time alignment for capacity reservation

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on our conversation I pulled together an updated mutual action plan (attached: MAP_draft_v2.pdf) that focuses on capacity reservation timing and measurable acceptance criteria so we can lock a Dedicated or Private reservation without surprises. High-level points: 

- Lead-time expectations: Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pool): typically 6–8 weeks from signed commitment to initial availability; Private (VPC / on-prem appliance): 10–14 weeks depending on on-prem hardware procurement and network validation.
- Recommended pilot sizing: start with an 8 A100-eq worker pool (or equivalent vCPU/VRAM profile) for functional and load validation; production ramp target = 32 A100-eq (adjust after eval metrics).
- Acceptance criteria (proposed):
  - Functional: model variant(s) serve inference requests end-to-end with prefix KV caching and tool calls integrated.
  - Performance: p50 latency <120ms, p95 <450ms for target prompt mix under concurrency test.
  - Cost/throughput checkpoint: per-token cost within 20% of estimated bench; autoscale triggers validated.
- Eval plan (summary): 2-week sandbox evaluation (Week 0–2): integration smoke tests + load test up to target concurrency; Week 3: decision/go/no-go.

Asks from your side:
1) Confirm whether Helium prefers Dedicated (hosted reserved) or Private (VPC/on-prem) — this materially changes lead times.
2) What production concurrency and qps should we size the pilot for? (example: 250 concurrent users / ~200 qps).
3) Who owns the security/compliance intake (SOC 2 / network review)? We can have Soojin own our evidence bundle.

If you’re aligned I can convert the MAP to a formal MSA amendment + reservation schedule and share next steps (DocuSign link) and a procurement checklist for your team. I added an internal calendar invite for a 30-minute handoff — pick a time here: https://cal.redwood.ai/rafael/30m

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Rafael —

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the MAP draft. A few constraints from our side that will affect which path we take: 

- Procurement calendar: our internal PO + vendor onboarding typically takes ~6 weeks once terms are agreed; if we require hardware procurement for on-prem it adds another 4–6 weeks (so Private total ~10–12 weeks realistic for us).
- Residency: initial environments must be in us-east (we can expand later).
- SOC 2: we need the SOC 2 report and evidence for API access — we’ll need a named contact and a security intake doc (can you provide your SOC 2 cert and a short evidence checklist?).

Regarding sizing — we can commit to a pilot of 12 A100-eq (Helium will fund pilot capacity). Our target steady-state for Q1 is closer to 28–36 A100-eq depending on model compression/quantization.

Question: is there an interim fallback to Redwood hosted (non-reserved) if Private provisioning slips? Also please highlight any cancellation / change windows on the reservation schedule.

I can loop procurement now if you send the reservation schedule and the minimal SOW / payment milestones.

Ben

Thanks Ben — and great questions. I’m attaching a concise eval test plan (eval_test_plan.xlsx) and below is an operationalized MAP timeline that maps to the lead times you called out.

Operational MAP (proposed timeline, compressed view):
- Week 0 (Day 0–7): Kickoff — access, networking baseline, SOC 2 evidence intake (Soojin to coordinate).
- Week 1–2: Sandbox eval — functional checks + integration smoke tests; load generator exercise at 50% target concurrency on day 10; collect p50/p95.
- Week 3: Production readiness review (internal go/no-go). If go -> sign reservation schedule and issue PO.
- Week 4–7: Procurement & provisioning for Dedicated (if Dedicated chosen): hardware pool allocation and staging; target initial availability by end of Week 7.
- Week 4–12: Procurement & on-prem validation for Private (if Private chosen): procurement, delivery, rack & network validation; target availability by Week 12 in typical case.
- Post-deploy Week 1–2: Acceptance run (traffic soak, canary, and final sign-off).

Acceptance gates (we make these measurable so procurement and engineering can sign off quickly):
- Gate A: Network connectivity + access auth (S0): basic smoke tests pass.
- Gate B: Functional routing + KV cache correctness (S1): integration smoke tests pass.
- Gate C: Performance gate (S2): p50/p95 within agreed thresholds under the defined load profile.
- Gate D: Security/compliance checklist completed (S3): SOC 2 doc delivered and basic audit items resolved.

Fallback options: yes — we can provision a temporary hosted (non-reserved) pool to cover production traffic for up to 30 days while Private provisioning completes; pricing and unit caps differ (I’ll include the temporary fallback schedule in the reservation schedule). Cancellation/change windows: we normally allow a 14-day window before provisioning for sizing changes without penalty; will note strict change windows in the SOW.

Next steps for action items (owners):
- Soojin Lee (security intake): deliver SOC 2 cert + evidence checklist to helium.security@heliumai.com by Tue 12/2.
- Rafael: share reservation schedule and SOW for procurement by EOD 11/30.
- Ben/Procurement: confirm PO timeline & procurement contact.

Ben — Rafael will send the formal reservation schedule + DocuSign link shortly. If Helium confirms the pilot 12 A100-eq, we will size the sandbox to simulate that concurrency and include the fallback hosted pool in the SOW.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
